M3_cpython_takes_bytecode_by_mtime_secon.rule: importlib validates a timestamp .pyc by the source's mtime in whole seconds and its size (a 32-bit field each)
M3_cpython_takes_bytecode_by_mtime_secon.measured: S2's developer writes app/calc.py at 32 bytes (a + b). The implementer's checkout is the developer's: calc.py dated at the developer's write, never rewritten by the kernel's forced checkouts (stat matches the index). The verifier's checkout dates calc.py at its own checkout (rewritten again at the move to the merged revision). Collision: the developer's write in the same second as S0's checkout (the bytecode's header second) while the verifier's checkout is in another second → implementer reads the stale bytecode (sub(3,1) == 2: SATISFIED), verifier compiles the source (4: REFUTED) → results differ under identical instrument identity and identical revision → VERIFIER_DISAGREEMENT at post-merge C0 → rollback

classification.statement: kernel/orchestration defect: the observation mechanism writes bytecode into the checkout it observes although the kernel configures it not to (M1), and the two-party proof's outcome depends on a property of the checkout the revision does not fix (file dates) whenever the revision carries bytecode of another source (M2, M3) — the proof is then not a function of the revision, and the same rule can mask a real post-merge regression (M6)
classification.co_factor_not_excusing_the_kernel: the test fixture's developer double commits __pycache__ (git add -A, no ignore rules): this is how the revision came to carry bytecode here; a real developer capability that commits __pycache__ produces the same revision, and the kernel has no defence against it. A fixture-only correction (an ignore rule) would remove the symptom from ORCH_9_and_10 and leave M1 and M3 in the kernel
classification.why_not_A: M1 is the kernel's own setting defeated by its own launch flag; M3 is a property of the kernel's proof, not of the test
classification.why_not_C: no environment or capability was absent; both parties executed; the OS and interpreter behaved as specified
classification.why_not_D: instrument identity (probe id, digest, enforcement, semantic hash) was identical in every captured disagreement; PROBE_MISMATCH did not apply
